tools.name: SuggestSkills
tools.description:
Render a card of standalone skills the user can add — org, shared, or Anthropic skills not yet enabled.

Call this when the task is one a skill could make repeatable — drafting in a house style, reviews against a playbook, a recurring workflow — and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about skills. Also when they ask for recommendations, or when ListSkills returned zero matches. Use ListSkills for skills they already have.

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a skill would help, or if you already rendered a suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

Pass keywords drawn from the task itself, and set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). If the result is empty and the trigger was proactive, continue the task without mentioning that you searched; if the user asked, tell them you found nothing new to add.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

schema.name: Write
schema.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__mark_chapter
tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'inspect' returns the accessibility tree of the front app (what a screen reader reads, which can differ from what is drawn) as JSON — per element: type, label, value, frame [x,y,width,height] in device points from the top-left, traits the type does not imply, enabled only when false, children. Call 'inspect' before a 'tap' on anything you have not located in this screen's tree, before answering what text a screen shows, and before reporting a control's state (a switch's value, whether a button is enabled, which tab is selected) or whether a sheet, alert or other modal is in front (the result says so) — never guess coordinates from memory of similar apps, and do not 'screenshot' for these. Go straight to 'screenshot' for color, images, and layout. Three reads: no marker and no x/y = the whole visible tree (the safe default when you do not know the exact label); marker = the first element, in tree order, whose label contains that CASE-SENSITIVE substring — a title can match before the button with the same text, so check the matched element's type; x/y = the element drawn on top at that point, as a tap would find it, with its descendants (a point between controls hits their container). If a marker misses or returns the wrong element, read the whole tree instead of guessing or screenshotting. Then tap the center of the target's frame. Hidden, off-screen, and illegibly small elements are omitted and counted; text longer than its area shows is cut (it ends with ...). Only the x/y read resolves occlusion, and only by bars and containers it can recognize: a frame from the whole-tree or marker read that overlaps a later sibling (a tab bar, a sheet) may be covered, so before tapping it read x/y at its center; a point on a sheet's blank area can still read the content behind it, so when the result reports a modal, stay inside it. A tree over the size cap loses its deepest levels first and says so — narrow with marker, or with x/y on the target itself: a point in a gap answers the container around it, which is no smaller; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the currently attached simulator, or the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000, total clamped to 30s).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

marker.description: For 'inspect': return only the first element (tree order, with its descendants) whose match_key attribute contains this case-sensitive substring — pass the label text exactly as the tree or the user wrote it, and prefer a distinctive fragment over a guess at capitalization. Omit for the whole tree (the safe default), or pass x/y instead for the element under a point.

content.content:
### M0: machinery every later milestone needs

- **Computation-only policy.** A registry declaration beside `ActionClass` that the coordinator honours; coordinator tests prove no card for `slice_start`, `activity_cancel`, `plan_set`, and a card for `slice_start` with `preempt: true`. Guide section "Computation-only mutations".
- **Output validator keywords.** Add `enum` and `maxLength` to `ToolRegistry::validate_output` with tests before any schema uses them. Guide section "Registry facts worth knowing".
- **JusPrin-owned stores.** Intent, plan, and region annotations in the 3mf auxiliary directory; confirmed printer facts in app data keyed by printer identity with expiry. Extend `ProjectStateDocument` ([ProjectStateDocument.hpp](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ProjectStateDocument.hpp)) rather than adding a second persistence path; it already handles load, migration, and corruption. Add change reasons `Intent`, `Plan`, `Regions`, `PrinterFacts` to `ProjectStateChangeReason` in [ProjectState.hpp](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectState.hpp) and include them in `kInvalidatingReasons`. Provenance vocabulary per the guide section "JusPrin-owned project state".
- **Output schemas off the MCP wire.** `McpProtocol.cpp` currently emits `outputSchema` for every tool ([McpProtocol.cpp:208](../../src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Mcp/McpProtocol.cpp)). Stop advertising it; keep `validate_output` on every MCP success. Update the protocol fixtures and the Python bridge tests. Measure the catalog bytes before and after with the offline helper (recipe below) and record both numbers in the PR.
- **Fixture retirement plan.** `duplicate_object`, `import_model`, and `inspect_selection` are removed in the PRs that land `plate_layout`, `object_import`, and the `summary` section's selection ids. Until then they keep their current inputs. Guide section "Input design".

### M1: the core loop on the existing project

Tools: `workspace_inspect` sections `summary`, `intent`, `plan`, `slicing`; `intent_update`; `plan_set`; `slice_start`; `slice_report` sections summary, Orca warnings, conflicts and toolpath outside the bed, material changes.

- `workspace_inspect` gains an optional `sections` input defaulting to `summary`, and `summary` keeps every field the tool returns today so existing callers and fixtures do not break. The `slicing` section is where action-handle state is read; there is no separate activity read.
- `slice_start` follows the guide's "Asynchronous operations" section exactly: start through `Plater`'s reslice path, return a handle, let `ToolActivity` track pending, running, terminal, and invalidated; completion and invalidation publish a change reason. Add a `Slicing` change reason if the existing set cannot express "slice result replaced or invalidated".
- `slice_report` is built from `Print` statistics and the `GCodeProcessor` result already on the plate. Supports, seams, first layer, islands, and intent checks come in M5 and M6 when regions and intent exist.

Eval: from Claude Code through `jusprin-mcp`, "slice the current plate and tell me the print time, filament use, and any warnings"; then change a setting in the GUI and ask again, which must show the stale state and a fresh slice.

### M2: project files and hardware setup

JusPrin Journey Tools

    JusPrin · handoff report · 17 Sep 2026

    Journey tools: from a model file to exported G-code

    The JusPrin agent, in the app and over MCP, now has the tools to take a project from an opened 3MF or imported STL to a G-code file, milestones M0 to M7 of the handoff. This report covers what was built, how it was tested, and where it still falls short.

      Branch claude/journey-tools-m0 (pushed)
      Base jusprin-newui · 49 commits ahead, 4 behind, merges cleanly
      Test printer in-process fake Bambu A1 mini
      Model OpenAI gpt-5.4-mini

    Where it stands

        MCP journey
        Pass

        Scripted client, every approval clicked in the JusPrin panel. Ran twice on the final build.

        In-app journey
        1 of 7

        Every run reached an exported file. One met the whole request; the rest exposed app bugs (fixed) or a model orientation choice.

        Automated tests
        All green

        211 agent cases, 133 page tests, workspace contract, Python bridge, and the shell harness in all four modes.

      Pull request not opened yet

      The GitHub CLI isn't installed on this machine, and the app's browser isn't signed in to GitHub. Open it from the compare page; a ready description is in the scratchpad as pr-body.md.

    Milestones

        MilestoneWhat the agent can now doEval

          M0Foundations: approval exemption for computation-only tools, intent and plan stored in the project, output validation for closed vocabularies, token baseline recorded.baseline

          M1Record what the print is for and the agent's plan; start a slice and read its report; list presets and printers.recorded

          M2Save and open projects and model files, with Orca's dialog questions answered from the request; restore undo history; set up printer, plate, process and filament with a preview; keep facts a person states about a printer.recorded

          M3Analyze an object's geometry (faces, holes, units, orientations), place it, lay out plates, import and delete. Three fixture tools retired.MCP pass in-app partial

          M4Change supports, adhesion, seam and speed settings, and one object's overrides.MCP pass in-app partial

          M5Mark what regions of an object mean (protect a hole, seam on a face) and have Orca print them that way; cut, split, merge and repair; check a slice for support in holes, seams on faces, first-layer contact and islands.MCP pass in-app 0 of 5

          M6Render a picture of the plate and read packed pictures (the model sees the image); inspect a slice's layers and G-code; cancel runs; export G-code, sliced 3MF, project, STL or presets after approval.MCP pass in-app pass

          M7Group several changes on one approval card with a shared planId; they run in order and stop together if one fails or the project changes underneath.live regression pass

    The catalog is 30 tool definitions in the app (36,195 bytes per turn) and 31 over MCP (40,714 bytes, two pages). The live regression ran 25 requests of 7,249 to 11,619 input tokens, 72 to 95 per cent cached after the first.

    Final journey eval

    The request, per the handoff: open a one-object STL (Orca's Cali Cat, 28.5 × 28.5 × 35 mm), say it is decorative, the front face will be visible, it must print in under five hours in PLA, and reach an exported G-code file with no manual setting edits and a slice without warnings.

    Over MCP pass

      Intent recorded, geometry analyzed, plan with decisions and assumptions recorded.

      One plan card held the face markings and the seam setting; both answered "queued", one click ran both.

      Slice: 1,824 s against the 18,000 s limit; 0 seams on the visible face, 274 of 296 on the hidden one; no warning that applies to a G-code print.

      Only the plan's own setting changed; the export was written after approval (950 KB). No dialog appeared.

    In the app, with OpenAI 1 of 7

      Runs 1–2The agent opened the STL by path, which ends the chat it came from, and the new project showed a card stuck on "running". A refusal also didn't say what was wrong. app bugs, fixed

      Run 3Tried to save the project over the .gcode path and skipped the plan step. app bug, fixed

      Runs 4, 5, 7Turned the cat onto its side (Orca's orientation score ranks that first), then exported a slice that warns of a floating cantilever. In run 7 the export card named the warning and the agent reported it. model choice

      Run 6Intent and plan recorded, import and slice approved on one card, cat left upright, 1,819 s, no warnings, no setting changes. pass

    Every run reached an exported file in two or three turns, with "Approved. Carry on." after each plan card. No run asked a question, which suits this model: nothing in its geometry makes a choice consequential.

    What the evals changed

      The slice report treats Bambu's print-dialog warnings the way Orca does: the bed-temperature one is dropped, the timelapse ones are marked as applying only to timelapse prints.

      An export card and its result list the slice's own warnings, so the person approving sees them.

      Saving the project to a non-.3mf path is refused before the card, pointing at the export tool.

      A plan's card stays disabled while the agent is still adding to it, and a decided or failed plan takes no new calls.

      plan_set no longer joins plans; a live run read "make these changes as one plan" as a call to it.

      Refused calls name the wrong values; the call that opened a project no longer shows in the project it opened.

      Both the in-app agent and MCP clients get one sentence on how a print request goes.

    Known limits

      In the app, the agent often trusts Orca's orientation score over the visible-face request and exports without reading the slice report. The tools report the problem truthfully; the model doesn't act on it.

      Opening a project from chat ends that chat, because the chat belongs to the closed project. In-app runs used an attached STL instead.

      The MCP eval used a scripted client in place of Claude Code, as instructed.

      After approving a plan, the person has to tell the agent to continue; the agent isn't woken when the plan finishes.

    Also on this branch

      00785d921d, from another session: chat titles come from the user's first message, fixing English chats titled in Chinese.

      c64461fdba, from another session: the Windows workspace adapter harness works again (617 checks).

      Earlier: the eight Windows MCP bridge test failures, fixed in another session and verified here.

      Refused calls name the wrong values; the call that opened a project no longer shows in the project it opened.

      Both the in-app agent and MCP clients get one sentence on how a print request goes.

    Known limits

      In the app, the agent often trusts Orca's orientation score over the visible-face request and exports without reading the slice report. The tools report the problem truthfully; the model doesn't act on it.

      Opening a project from chat ends that chat, because the chat belongs to the closed project. In-app runs used an attached STL instead.

      The MCP eval used a scripted client in place of Claude Code, as instructed.

      After approving a plan, the person has to tell the agent to continue; the agent isn't woken when the plan finishes.

    Also on this branch

      00785d921d, from another session: chat titles come from the user's first message, fixing English chats titled in Chinese.

      c64461fdba, from another session: the Windows workspace adapter harness works again (617 checks).

      Earlier: the eight Windows MCP bridge test failures, fixed in another session and verified here.

content.content:
---
name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-14T14:18:48.216Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.
---
name: liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit
description: "RelWithDebInfo liblibslic3r_gui.a crossed Apple ar's 4 GiB archive limit on jusprin-newui (2026-09-13); CMAKE_AR override is ignored; manual llvm-ar relink recipe and its cd trap"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 0771473f-5d46-4419-b8e5-112938ea6b34
  modified: 2026-09-14T14:18:50.456Z
---

On 2026-09-13, at jusprin-newui 770bd2b0a2 (after "Add the evidence-led Add a
printer flow"), a worktree RelWithDebInfo build failed archiving
`src/slic3r/RelWithDebInfo/liblibslic3r_gui.a`:
`Assertion failed: (memberOffset < 0xFFFFFFFF) ... ArchiveWriter.cpp` then
`fatal error in .../ranlib`. The archive llvm-ar produced was 4,309,350,176
bytes; the main checkout's copy built minutes earlier was 4,143,827,796 and
still fit. Objects are big because the root CMakeLists.txt (lines ~544-548)
rewrites RelWithDebInfo -O2 to -O0 on purpose. Disk space was not the cause.

**Why:** the failed build left the OLD harness binary in place, and the harness
runs afterwards "passed" against stale code (a new `--printer-setup` flag
silently ran the default mode: same 285 check count). Gate runs on build
success and compare binary mtime.

**How to apply:**
- `-DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar` on an existing build dir does
  nothing: `CMakeFiles/<ver>/CMakeCXXCompiler.cmake` sets CMAKE_AR as a normal
  variable that shadows the cache.
- Working relink: `ninja -f build-RelWithDebInfo.ninja -t commands <target>`,
  drop compile lines, swap ar/ranlib for llvm-ar/llvm-ranlib on the gui archive
  line only, then run EACH line in its own `(cd build/arm64 && eval "$line")`.
  One `sh` script fails with bogus "no such file" errors because the
  encoding-check line does `cd src/slic3r` and it leaks; `sh -e` also does not
  stop inside `&&` chains. Apple's linker accepted the >4 GiB llvm-ar archive.
- The fix is PER BUILD DIRECTORY, nothing in the repo selects llvm-ar. Main

name: background-bash-timeout-kills-builds
description: "A run_in_background Bash build dies at the tool timeout (ninja prints \"interrupted by user\", exit 130); launch long builds with nohup and watch the log instead"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 8c1e8dd3-1475-48e9-9398-2d5eaa424bab
  modified: 2026-09-14T19:01:34.576Z
---

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-09-09T16:51:11.156Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

On 2026-09-08, three subagents launched with `isolation: "worktree"` got
worktrees at 095fb66576, an old commit with no JusPrin shell code, not the
branch tip they were told to expect. All three stopped correctly. SendMessage

give the agent the absolute path and the expected SHA, and tell it to stop if
HEAD differs. Tell every agent the shell cwd may reset to the main checkout,
so all paths must be absolute. Before landing on `jusprin-newui`, read
`git reflog show jusprin-newui --date=relative`; if it moved in the last few
minutes another session is rebasing it. Land by cherry-pick, never
fast-forward, and expect your own commits to have new hashes afterwards.

metadata:

  originSessionId: 28d33b5a-3e97-48b6-8eaf-5192f6d7d30d
  modified: 2026-09-10T20:04:58.544Z
---

On 2026-09-10 a measurement subagent kicked off a 700-step JusPrin rebuild in
the background, then ended its turn with "I'll wait for the completion
notification." Subagents get no notifications after they stop, and SendMessage
was unavailable, so the parent had to babysit the ninja PID and run the
harness itself.

**Why:** a subagent's turn is its whole life. Anything it defers to "later"
never happens. The parent cannot resume it without SendMessage.

**How to apply:** in every Agent prompt for work that includes a build or any
long step, say explicitly: run long commands in the foreground with a long
timeout (up to 600000 ms per call, loop `until` the PID exits if longer), and
never end the turn while a step is still running or a result is still
pending. If the agent stops early anyway, check `ps` for its build process,
wait on the PID, and finish its plan from its scratch files. See
[[subagent-worktrees-create-manually]] and [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-14T14:18:48.216Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

  4,308,513,464 bytes). Shortcut that worked: after the failed build, from
  `-t commands shell_integration_harness` drop lines containing ` -c `; only
  the last two remain relevant (gui archive, then harness link). Run just
  those two, swapping ar/ranlib on the archive line. Harness then passed.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

`jusprin-newui` (the current working branch as of 2026-09-16) carries an in-process fake Bambu printer, landed as two commits: `7acf075aaa` (implementation, 2026-09-08 10:57) and `e04c0d40d3` (docs, 2026-09-08 11:00). Both are `Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>` — done by a Cursor agent on worktree branch `cursor/cd073db7` (created from `a9adaae973`), then cherry-picked onto `jusprin-newui` (parent `367f5703b3`). Operator guide: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md`.

**Design:** unlike the Moonraker simulator ([[fake-moonraker-printer-sim]], which fakes the wire protocol and lives on a different branch entirely), this keeps a real Bambu Lab **system** preset selected (so `PresetBundle::is_bbl_vendor()` stays true and every Bambu-only UI gate passes) and substitutes only the printer-agent implementation, at the `NetworkAgentFactory` factory level, under id `jusprin-fake-bambu`. Two earlier attempts (`a162493544`, `3c244108b4`, both reverted same day) tried faking a *non-Bambu* agent or patching the header chip directly — both failed because Bambu-only gates rejected them or because it only patched a symptom. Faking Bambu's real network (MQTT/TLS 8883, FTPS 990, discovery) was evaluated and explicitly rejected as out of scope.

**The seam:** exactly 4 added lines in `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent` (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:3574-3579`, 1 include + 3 body lines) — inside the existing `if (preset_bundle->is_bbl_vendor())` branch, `fake_bambu_printer_agent_id(app_config)` overrides `effective_agent_id` when fake mode is on, otherwise the branch is untouched. No upstream line deleted.

**Config surface is a JSON file only, no MCP tools** (Kenneth's explicit call): turn it on via `"jusprin": {"fake_printer": true}` in `JusPrin2.conf` (JSON booleans store as the string `"true"`; an INI `[jusprin]` block is silently ignored), then drive live state by writing `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (reread ~1s) with `state`/`progress`/`nozzle`/`bed`/`offline` keys. The C++ parameter carrying the datadir into the agent is misleadingly named `log_dir` (an upstream `NetworkAgentFactory::PrinterAgentFactory` convention, documented as "Directory for log files") — verified it's actually `data_dir()` at the call site, not a log subdirectory; don't be misled by the name when reading the code.

Emulates printer type `N1` (`JUSPRIN_FAKE_BAMBU_PRINTER_TYPE`), device id `FAKE001`, shows as **JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)** in Select Machine. Idle/Printing/Offline is the printer-menu **first row** (opened by clicking the printer half of the chip), never on the chip itself. The heartbeat thread does not start in the constructor — only in `set_queue_on_main_fn` when a real callback is set — so unit tests that never wire that callback stay quiet. Test target: `jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` (`tests/jusprin/test_fake_bambu_agent.cpp`), coexists with `shell_theme_tests` in the same CMakeLists (their merge was a conflict the cherry-pick resolved by keeping both).

Doc pointers added in the two landing commits: `AGENTS.md`, `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`, `agent-docs/jusprin/engineering-method.md` ("Printer tests without hardware" section), `agent-docs/jusprin/orca-integration-guide.md`. A planning handoff doc (`agent-docs/jusprin/fake-bambu-printer-handoff.md`) was never committed and doesn't exist in the tree — don't look for it.

**Why:** Kenneth wants Bambu-path testing (header menu state, Select Machine, print job) without hardware, on the branch he actually works on day to day — distinct from the Moonraker/Klipper simulator, which stays on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` and covers the print-host HTTP path instead.

description: "Agent tool isolation:\"worktree\" cut worktrees from a stale base and SendMessage was disabled; create worktrees by hand on the intended commit and pass absolute paths"
metadata:

---

On 2026-09-08, three subagents launched with `isolation: "worktree"` got
worktrees at 095fb66576, an old commit with no JusPrin shell code, not the
branch tip they were told to expect. All three stopped correctly. SendMessage
was disabled in that session, so they could not be redirected; relaunching
was the only option.

**Why:** the isolation worktree is not cut from the current worktree's HEAD.
And `jusprin-newui` is rebased by other sessions while work is in flight, so
"base on newui" must be a specific commit, not a branch name.

**How to apply:** `git worktree add <path> -b <branch> <sha>` yourself, then
give the agent the absolute path and the expected SHA, and tell it to stop if
HEAD differs. Tell every agent the shell cwd may reset to the main checkout,
so all paths must be absolute. Before landing on `jusprin-newui`, read
`git reflog show jusprin-newui --date=relative`; if it moved in the last few
minutes another session is rebasing it. Land by cherry-pick, never
fast-forward, and expect your own commits to have new hashes afterwards.
See [[bash-cwd-resets-after-background]] and [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

name: subagent-must-not-stop-to-wait
description: "A background subagent that \"waits for the build notification\" ends its turn and is gone; tell agents to block on long builds in the foreground and never end a turn with work pending."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 28d33b5a-3e97-48b6-8eaf-5192f6d7d30d
  modified: 2026-09-10T20:04:58.544Z
---

On 2026-09-10 a measurement subagent kicked off a 700-step JusPrin rebuild in
the background, then ended its turn with "I'll wait for the completion
notification." Subagents get no notifications after they stop, and SendMessage
was unavailable, so the parent had to babysit the ninja PID and run the
harness itself.

**Why:** a subagent's turn is its whole life. Anything it defers to "later"
never happens. The parent cannot resume it without SendMessage.

**How to apply:** in every Agent prompt for work that includes a build or any
long step, say explicitly: run long commands in the foreground with a long
timeout (up to 600000 ms per call, loop `until` the PID exits if longer), and
never end the turn while a step is still running or a result is still
pending. If the agent stops early anyway, check `ps` for its build process,
wait on the PID, and finish its plan from its scratch files. See
[[subagent-worktrees-create-manually]] and [[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]].

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

When an event lands that the user would want to act on now — an error appeared, the status they were waiting on flipped — send a PushNotification. Not every event is worth a push; the ones that change what they'd do next are.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

870-On 2026-09-16 it failed on Windows: `select_object(0)` returned false after `load_files`, seven checks failed, and the process died with `0xC0000005`. The test code was not stale. The cause was the machine setup. The Mesa provisioning script put `opengl32.dll` only in `mesa\`, where only the app launcher looks for it. A harness has no launcher, so this one ran on the system's GL 1.1 and its canvas never initialized. Selection is built from the canvas's volumes, so nothing could be selected, and the gizmo check then opened a paint gizmo with nothing selected. The script now also copies `opengl32.dll` beside each harness (see "Software GL on Windows machines without a GPU" in [engineering-method.md](engineering-method.md)); re-run it on existing build trees. With GL in place, two harness faults surfaced that only Windows shows:
871-
872-- The move-event check asserted that the move was the last change. On Windows, queued `EVT_GLCANVAS_OBJECT_SELECT` events publish two Selection-only changes after it, so the check now skips those.
873-- The data-directory cleanup threw, because the open log file cannot be deleted, and the uncaught exception turned a PASS into `0xC0000409`. It now warns instead, as the shell harness already did.
874-
875-Pulling the script change does not fix a build tree that was already provisioned; run the script on it again. So that a tree without GL cannot fail this way unnoticed again, the harness now checks, right after its first model load, that the canvas initialized GL. If it did not, the harness stops with `HARNESS ERROR the 3D canvas did not initialize OpenGL` and the command to fix it, exits 1, and does not crash. A clean exit on that early path also needed the harness to close the main frame, as the shell harness does. It used to call `ExitMainLoop()`, which skips `MainFrame::shutdown()`, and a pending project backup then posted to the deleted frame.
876-
877-Node is required: the Agent and Home pages are built from TypeScript and their `index.html` is generated, not committed, so a tree without npm fails at configure time and an app built without them shows no Agent panel at all.

## Findings, most serious first

**1. Slice state changes break plans, and a card-free `slice_start` fails the user's pending cards.** (confirmed by reading)
- The adapter publishes `WorkspaceChangeReasons::Plates` whenever a plate's slice state changes (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter.cpp:252`, not new on this branch). The coordinator treats `Plates` as an invalidating change (`ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:29-31`).
- **Plan scenario:** a plan contains `slice_start` with `wait` followed by any later member.
  - The slice finishes asynchronously, when `m_executing` is empty, so `invalidate_pending` (`:2083-2089`) adds the plan to `m_disturbed_plans`.
  - The next member then fails `stale_revision` at `:960-965`, even though the change came from the plan's own step.
- **Non-plan scenario:** any pending card fails as soon as a slice the agent started without a card finishes, including `intent_update`, `plate_layout`, or an export for another plate.
- **G-code export cannot be a later plan step at all.** `check_export` refuses unless a current slice already exists (`OrcaOutputs.cpp:330`).
  - If the plate is already sliced, the export card shows warnings (`:469`) from the slice the plan is about to replace.
  - The fake workspace also publishes `Plates` when a slice finishes (`FakeWorkspace.hpp:1045`), so a test of "slice then export" in one plan would fail today. No such test exists.

  - "Approve all" there also runs the in-app members, which were never shown on that card. That is an approval bypass.
- **Across chats:** `planMembers` (`PlanActivityCard.tsx`) groups over every activity. A plan id reused while an older plan is still pending renders under the old message, and the new chat shows no card at all.

**3. A plan member that fails or is cancelled before approval leaves the other members approvable.** (confirmed)
- `fail()` cascades only to members that are Approved or Running (`:2047-2051`), and `cancel()` does not cascade at all (`:801-815`).
- **Scenario:** a plan of settings patch, then slice, then export, where the export fails at proposal (as in finding 1).
  - The plan is marked closed to new members, but the first two members stay pending. "Approve all" runs them, and the user gets a partial plan.
- The same happens when an `activity_cancel` (no card, and able to target another source's proposal, `:1436-1440`) cancels one pending member.
- The spec asks that a plan stop on failure.

**4. `m_disturbed_plans` is never cleared.** (confirmed)
- Neither `clear()` nor `forget_terminal_activities` resets it, and neither resets `m_slice_handle`.
- Once a plan id has been disturbed, a later plan reusing that id passes the "closed" check (its old records are gone after a project open or chat deletion). That later plan then fails `stale_revision` on its first member, for the rest of the app session.
- `forget_if_closed`'s own comment says action ids start again in the new project, so the stale `m_slice_handle` can also collide with a new action id in `activity_cancel`.

**5. Card titles are cut mid-character and can hide the path.** (UTF-8 split confirmed; that it throws is from nlohmann's default behaviour)
- Every new title truncation in `propose()` (`:393, 406, 416, 510, 544, 581, 613, 656, 687, 712, 736`) and in `ToolRegistry.cpp:1542,1558` uses `resize(kToolLabelLimit - 3)`. That can split a multi-byte UTF-8 character. `ToolResults.cpp:19-20` already has a helper that doesn't.
- `AgentHost::send_envelope` dumps with nlohmann's default strict error handler, which throws on invalid UTF-8.
- **Scenario:** a CJK folder name or object name near the 256-byte limit throws while the card is being sent.
- Separately, paths may be up to 1024 bytes (`ToolRegistry.cpp:340`) but titles stop at 256. For `project_open`, `project_save`, `object_import_file` and `export_file`, the card then does not show the exact path the spec requires. On an export card the licence restriction and the slice warnings are cut off completely.

**6. MCP plan cards can be approved while the client is still adding members.** (confirmed)
- `App.tsx` never passes `stillProposing` for external plans. The native side refuses later members with `plan_closed`, so approving mid-sequence runs a partial plan.
- In-app plans are guarded only by the page (`streamingMessageId !== null`); the native side does not enforce it.

**7. Lower severity.**
- The export card's "replacing it" is checked at proposal (`:465`). A file created before approval is overwritten without the card saying so, whenever `overwrite` is true.
- `OpenAIResponsesAgent::continue_after_tool` stores the image in `m_input_history`, so each picture of up to 2 MB is re-sent on every later request in that turn. This matters for the token numbers the spec asks you to record.

## Checked and fine
- **Exemption scope:** only `plan_set`, `slice_start` and `activity_cancel` are exempt. `preempt: true` brings the card back (`ToolRegistry.cpp:1523-1534`), and destructive tools never qualify.
- **Paths before approval:** `project_open` and `object_import_file` only check that the file exists. `project_save` binds `resolvedPath` at proposal. `export_file` writes only in `execute`.
- **MCP annotations:** `readOnlyHint` is false for the exempt tools. The output schema is gone from the wire but still validated on every success.
- **Memory safety:** `project_open` looks its record up again after `clear()`. `pump()` returns right after `execute`, so no reference is left dangling.
- **Exception handling:** no exception is swallowed anywhere in my area.

## Tests (`tests/agent/test_tool_coordinator.cpp`)
- **M0 is covered:**
  - No card for `plan_set` (`:585`).
  - No card for `slice_start` (around `:670`).
  - No card for `activity_cancel` (`:2032`).
  - A card for `slice_start` with `preempt` (`:709-711`).
  - The exact list of exempt tools (`:128`).
- **M7 has one test (`:2101`) with these gaps:**
  - A failure partway through, after an earlier member succeeded.
  - A member that fails at proposal.
  - A plan that contains `slice_start` with `wait` (would expose finding 1).
  - Plan ids shared across sources or chats (finding 2).
  - Plan id reuse after `clear()` (finding 4).
  - Cancelling one member.
  - The "outside change" section only covers a change before the first member runs.</result>

<task-notification>
<task-id>a5e1fbc53dae96a5b</task-id>
<tool-use-id>REDACTED</tool-use-id>
<output-file>/private/tmp/claude/claude-502/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/d5d144e4-a594-430e-b195-519b492dc2c1/tasks/a5e1fbc53dae96a5b.output</output-file>
